item.title: LAB: Western Front lines, First World War (data for lessons) v0.2
item.snippet: Test layer: dated Western Front lines traced from public-domain maps, for the time slider: the furthest German advance in September 1914, the front from late 1914 to March 1917, the front from March 1917 to March 1918, and the front at the Armistice. Draft.
item.description:
Test layer. Western Front lines, each with the dates it shows: the furthest German advance in September 1914 (before the Battle of the Marne), the front from late 1914 to March 1917, the front from March 1917 (after the German withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line) to March 1918, and the front at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918. The German offensives of spring 1918 and the Allied advance of summer and autumn 1918 are not in this version.

For the time slider: use ShowFrom as the start field and ShowTo as the end field. Kind tells front lines from the furthest-advance line. Each line's Description says what it shows and what it leaves out.

How they were made: traced from the coloured lines on two maps and placed on the ground using towns. Usually within about 2 to 4 km of the source maps' lines (AccuracyKm), so they suit maps of Europe or a region, not close-up maps of villages. A US Army map of the front on 21 March 1918 agrees with the March 1917 to March 1918 line to within about 3 km.

Sources: The Western Theatre of the European War, 1918 edition, by B. Barrecchia, Société Editrice Géographique, Paris (Harry S. Truman Library & Museum, M1236). Order of Battle on Western Front, 11 A.M., Nov. 11, 1918, G-3, GHQ, American Expeditionary Forces (Library of Congress). Checked against front lines as of March 21, 1918, Map Room, G-3, GHQ, AEF (Truman Library, M549).

Data version 0.2 (26 November 2026), lab draft.
